headline: 🔥 THE TOP-OF-LIST AGENT IS NOW FOUR DAYS UNCALLED — Amy G. filed Saturday night: interested YES, both price fields blank, "my buyers really like the property and have put it at the top of their list," and a full Monday has come and gone. ⚠️ THE SHOWING FEED HAS BEEN COMPLETELY SILENT FOR 42 HOURS across eight listings, with nothing booked ahead — and 198 Rena came OFF the board entirely today, cancelled by Gene at 1:13 PM.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 AMY G. OF ETHOS INTERNATIONAL FILED SATURDAY AT 11:24 PM off that afternoon's 1:00 PM tour: interested — YES, staged 3, and in her own words — "My buyers have just started looking. They really like the property and have put it at the top of their list." ⭐ SHE LEFT BOTH PRICE FIELDS BLANK, which makes this the FIFTH consecutive read since the 8/5 cut where nobody argued the number. ⭐ And she is the same agent who phoned from inside the house mid-showing — the channel is already open and warm. ⏰ THIS IS DAY THREE AND A FULL BUSINESS DAY HAS NOW PASSED ON IT. Four ShowingTime sweeps since have returned nothing new on any listing, so this has not been overtaken by a better signal — there is no other signal. It is still the single best thing on the board and still the oldest unworked one.
hotSignals.action: CALL her. Two things in one conversation: answer the basement lights (the half of her phone question you never got back to — the garage half you already answered by text), and ask what she would change about the staging, since she scored it a 3 and is the only agent to score staging at all since the cut. Quote $295,000 only. ⛔ Call, don't email — co-op agents remain the no-email lane and the ruling that would change that is now ten days open.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 AMBER G. OF KELLER WILLIAMS HOOVER: interested — YES, priced right — JUST RIGHT, staging 5 of 5, the highest score this listing has ever recorded. This was the FIRST read filed after the 8/5 price cut and it is the strongest pricing evidence the file carries. ⭐ Corroborated the same hour by a direct text to Gene asking whether the ceiling stains came from a previous leak — a question that is still unanswered a week later.
hotSignals.action: Answer the ceiling-stain question in writing — an unanswered condition question from an agent whose buyer said YES is the cheapest way to lose one. Then ask directly whether her buyer is still looking.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 WANDA W. OF MILLENNIUM HOMES answered the interest question with the single word "Very" and left every other field blank — off one of three tours filed within ninety minutes of each other on 8/8. ⚠️ THE ENTHUSIASM IS ON RECORD AND THE REASON IS NOT, which is exactly what makes it a phone call rather than an email. ⭐ Banked from the same three-form burst and still governing this listing: the objection is SIZE, not price — verified three ways, clearest being "Just too small."
hotSignals.action: Call her and find out what "Very" means — is her buyer still active, and what would need to be true. ⛔ Do not offer price: no discount reaches a size objection. Nine days of decay on the only enthusiastic read this listing has ever produced.

upcoming: 🆕 TOMORROW AFTERNOON, TUE 8/18 — 225 WILLOW POINT: the BUY-side showing that has never been worked. At 3:17 PM today Gene asked Sondra whether tomorrow afternoon works to go see the property she is interested in, and in the same message told them the listing agreement had come through and offered to cover questions on it while they're together. ⭐ THIS IS THE TWO-SIDED DEAL FINALLY BEING WORKED AS ONE APPOINTMENT — the LIST half executed Friday, the BUY half had never been touched by anyone until this afternoon. ⚠️ Not yet confirmed back, and no buyer criteria or budget exists anywhere in the system — tomorrow is also the intake.

⏰ THU 8/20, 3:00 PM — 5167 LAKE CREST CIR closing, at the closing attorney's office. Not a ShowingTime event, but it is the nearest hard date on the board and the largest number closing this month. Three days out with zero traffic on the file — worth one confirmation call tomorrow rather than an assumption. ⚠️ The funds land AFTER this week, not during it.

✅ HELD TODAY — 225 Willow Point photo shoot, and the Lay Lake listing walk-through at 10:30 AM that the seller asked for himself Sunday evening. Neither was a ShowingTime event and the Lay Lake one was on no calendar anywhere but this board; both are now behind you. What remains on Willow Point is the MLS input prep, the only step between that house and the market this weekend.

📭 NO SHOWINGS BOOKED, AND THE FEED HAS BEEN SILENT FOR 42 HOURS. There is not one future showing, walk-through, inspection or appraisal confirmed on any listing. The last tour was Saturday 4:00 PM at Ridge Trail; the newest ShowingTime notice of any kind is still Saturday night's Comanche feedback. ⭐ Said plainly because an empty row reads like a data problem and this is not one — the notices were pulled again this evening and the forward calendar is genuinely clear. ⚠️ Four days with no new booking is itself the finding, and today it got worse rather than better: the board went from eight actives to seven.

listings.note: 🆕 THE FEEDBACK GAP GOT AN ACTUAL FIX TODAY AND IT CAME FROM THE SELLER'S SIDE. At 3:08 PM the institutional seller asked that showing feedback be routed to them directly through the showing platform, to take the back-and-forth off Gene's plate; he forwarded it at 3:09 and the operations manager confirmed it done at 3:27. ⭐ THAT IS THE RIGHT NEWS ON THIS PARTICULAR FILE — three showings deep with not one word returned is the single biggest information gap on the board, and the fix landed inside twenty minutes without Gene touching it. ⚠️ It does not retrieve the three reads already missed. ✅ THE PRICE IS NOW INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED AND QUOTABLE at $550,000 — both Saturday notices print it. Every prior notice printed $559,000 because they all predated the cut. ⭐ THE TIMING IS THE POINT: the cut went live 8/13 and produced two tours inside forty-eight hours, six hours apart on the same Saturday, taking the all-time counter from 41 to 42 in a single day. That is the market answering the price question directly. 🔴 THE THREE-WEEK-OLD ITEM IS STILL THE ONE THAT WOULD MOVE THE NEEDLE: the 7/23 read said dirty plus GLITCHING ELECTRICAL, and the 8/4 read scored staging 2 of 5. The house did not get more expensive between those visits — it got less presentable. An electrician and a cleaner remain cheaper than another lost buyer. ⚠️ The live 8/10 social post still carries $559,000.

listings.note: 🛑 THE DECISION THIS BOARD CARRIED FOR FOUR DAYS WAS MADE BY GENE AT 1:13 PM TODAY, AND IT WAS NO. His note to the seller is unambiguous: the listing expires this evening, the sign gets picked up today or tomorrow, Don is grabbing the lockbox, everyone who had expressed interest has been told it is off the market, and all ads and media are stopped. ⭐ THE SHOWING RECORD SUPPORTS THE CALL, WHICH IS WHY IT BELONGS ON THIS BOARD RATHER THAN JUST IN THE FILE: two tours in the fourteen-day window and NOT ONE FORM RETURNED from either. Across the listing's whole life it produced exactly two feedback forms, and both left EVERY price field blank — 7/31 "Upstairs bathroom was a deal breaker because of the kids" and 7/12 "She LOVED the yard and lot" with the interior called too compartmentalized. ⭐ THAT IS THE UNUSUAL SHAPE WORTH REMEMBERING: 92 days, one written offer, and not a single agent who ever walked it argued the price. A house nobody objects to the price on, that nobody buys, has a positioning problem — and this seller was not going to change the layout. ⚠️ THE 8/11 'FULL-PRICE SHOWING' this board carried for two days never happened, by the showing agent's own admission. The 8/13 second-showing request from the same agent contradicted his own text that morning and was never confirmed. ⚠️ MACHINE LOOSE ENDS, NOT GENE'S: the milestone engine still carries this address as OFFER_RECEIVED, and 'we have stopped all ads and media' has not been shown to the marketing lane.

The inspection-response letter was never unsent — Gene sent it himself Saturday at 9:54 — and the document in the drafts folder was a DUPLICATE created six minutes later. Tonight's scan finds the drafts folder empty, so the duplicate is gone with everything else in it. ⭐ THE SHAPE OF THE BUYER'S ASK IS THE STORY: seventy-one items inspected, sixty-eight flagged at some level, and then exactly three requested. That is a reasonable buyer. ⭐ The recommendation sent is two yeses and a hold — agree to the basement leak and a scoped HVAC service, and on the roof ask for a few days and your own licensed roofer's report, because the inspector wrote that he cannot determine the roof's age or remaining life. ⚠️ FHA, so the appraiser can raise the roof independently and the concession room is small — this gets solved with work, not a check. 🔴 The date the buyers' repair-resolution window actually closes does not exist anywhere in this system. ⭐ Closing 10/23.

listings.note: 🔥 NO SHOWINGS, BUT THE HIGHEST LEAD YIELD IN THE PORTFOLIO BY A WIDE MARGIN — a new buyer came off the 19-lot ad at 4:31 PM today and was answered inside the hour, the ninth name off this one ad and the third in three days, while every other ad in the portfolio has produced zero. ✅ The 19-lot plat was located Friday and delivered — the exact document the open buyer chip had been waiting on. 🔴 THE HANDOFF IS THE PROBLEM, NOT THE COUNTY, AND IT IS DAY FIVE: the builder asked the septic perc question on 8/12, the operations manager researched and answered it completely, and that answer has sat on her board since Friday with nobody reading it back to him. The work was done; the delivery never happened. ⭐ THE PERC QUESTION IS PRICED, NOT BLOCKED: the county takes record searches in person only, weekdays 8:00–3:30, at a per-record fee — nineteen lots is a four-figure errand. So the choice is three-way: send someone for all nineteen, narrow to the lots a buyer is actually asking about, or ask the developer first, who almost certainly already holds the perc results from platting. ⭐ PERC DECIDES BUILDABILITY AND BUILDABILITY DECIDES PRICE PER LOT.

oweFeedback.when: 🔴 THREE ASKS AND TWENTY-SEVEN DAYS OF SILENCE — 7/21, 7/22 and 7/23, from the RealtySouth Inverness listing side after the 7/21 1:00 PM tour. ⭐ THIS IS THE ONE THAT COSTS SOMETHING REAL, and the cost is not the courtesy — it is that the honest written answer IS the counter on the largest number on the board, roughly $36K of GCI. The listing side has asked repeatedly to be moved forward; a seller who reverse-offers a buyer is a seller who wants a deal. Twenty minutes of writing moves it. ⚠️ The appraisal figure the buyer cited as far under ask is single-sourced from him — do not quote it to the other side as an appraised value.
